, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

Petitioners are knocking at the doors of Writ Court seeking quashment of order dated 07.1.2012 (Annexure A) passed by the 2nd Respondent - Deputy Commissioner, whereby the LRs of the original grantee are claiming compensation for the subject land.

2. BREIF FACTS:
(a) On 28.06.1964 the subject land was granted in favour of the father of the 5th Respondent herein.
Petitioner's father bought this property on 03.12.1969 by virtue of a Registered Sale Deed dated 03.12.1969; khatha was transferred and taxes are also paid.

Subsequently, LRs of the original grantee i.e., the private Respondents instituted Resumption proceedings under Section 5 of the Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prohibition of Transfer of Certain Lands) Act,
1978, alleging violation of statutory prohibition on transfer enacted therein.

sentences.text: (b) The 3rd Respondent - Assistant Commissioner having dismissed the remand on 12.11.2010

,
matter
was taken in appeal (Appeal No.129/2010-11) by the LRs of the 5th Respondent herein.
Subsequently, appeal was allowed by the Deputy Commissioner on 07.01.2012 directing resumption.

In the meanwhile, the subject property was acquired under the provisions of Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966 and now the resumption of land is challenged in this Writ Petition so that Petitioners can avail compensation in lieu of the land.

3. CONTENTION OF PARTIES:
(a) Learned counsel for the Petitioners placing reliance upon VIVEK M. HINDUJA &
OTHERS Vs. M. ASHWATHA & OTHERS, 2018(1) KAR L.R. 176 (SC) submits that in light of the law declared by the Apex Court no resumption could have been granted since even when no period for limitation is prescribed under the 1978 Act, the resumption ought to have been sought for within a reasonable period and that having not happened in this case, the impugned order of resumption has to be voided.

entities.text:
VIVEK M. HINDUJA &
OTHERS Vs. M. ASHWATHA & OTHERS, 2018(1) KAR L.R. 176 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So contending, he seeks indulgence of the Writ Court.

(b) Learned advocates appearing for the LRs of the original grantee oppose the Petition making submission in justification of the impugned order made by the 2nd Respondent - Deputy Commissioner in Appeal.

They add, the policy of State as enacted in the 1978 Act needs to be given effect, to its fullest extent regard being had to the interest of the oppressed classes and therefore,
Petition has to be dismissed so that the LRs of the grantee can take compensation payable for the subject land that is since acquired by the KIADB.
4.

Having heard the leaned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition papers, this Court is inclined to grant indulgence in the matter broadly agreeing with the submission made on behalf of the Petitioners.

It has been a well settled position of law from the days of Lord Halsbury that when a statute permits/ordains something to be done without prescribing a limitation,
ordinarily, such things shall be accomplished within a reasonable time.
An argument to the contrary would breed more public mischief than otherwise.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner is more than justified in banking upon the decision of the Apex Court in NEKKANTI RAMA LAKSHMI vs. SATE OF KARNATAKA & ANOTHER, 2018 (1) KAR L.R.
5 (SC) which is animated with the aforementioned long standing rule of law imbibed by all civilized jurisdictions.

entities.text:
NEKKANTI RAMA LAKSHMI vs. SATE OF KARNATAKA & ANOTHER, 2018 (1) KAR L.R.
5 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is also force in the submission of learned counsel for the Petitioners that since the land is already acquired for the benefit of KIADB, the compensation is payable to his clients only.
He is right in saying that payment is interdicted by the interim orders of this Court and therefore, a direction be issued to release the compensation in favour of the Petitioners.
In view of the above, this Writ Petition succeeds; a Writ of Certiorari issues quashing the impugned order of the 2nd Respondent - Deputy Commissioner (Annexure-A).

Consequently, KIADB is Sri Kothanur M Thammanna vs The State Of Karnataka on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186005117/
4 directed to release the compensation in favour of the Petitioners after ascertaining their credentials within a period of 8 weeks, failing which interest at the rate of 2% per month shall be payable on the amount due.
